E1.evidence: Issue #1311 (opened by a ros2_control maintainer, saikishor) gives printed values showing the controller node clock jumping from system time to sim time and the resulting unpublished state topic, plus before/after screenshots; the fix PR #1293 states "Fixes: https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1311" and was merged (master 5d4f6e72, humble backport #1332 merged as fe5b4f16).

E2.evidence: The controller plugin (joint_trajectory_controller, ros2_controllers) and its host (controller_manager, ros2_control) are separate units. At the broken revision the controller_manager creates the controller node through controller.c->init(controller.info.name, get_namespace()) and only afterwards applies the use_sim_time parameter with controller.c->get_node()->set_parameter(use_sim_time); the controller's node clock is therefore system time when the controller stamps last_state_publish_time_, and later switches to the simulation clock. The time source of the controller node (a value crossing the host/plugin boundary through the use_sim_time parameter) is wrong for the first cycles; the resolving edit is inside controller_manager (pass use_sim_time as a NodeOptions argument at node creation). Not deployment wiring (the change is in controller_manager code, not in a launch/config name binding), not build, not firmware.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the controller_manager's output (the use_sim_time parameter it applies to the controller node it creates) feeds the controller's input (its node clock, read by get_node()->now() in publish_state). The failure was observed when the controllers are loaded and started by the controller_manager in the TIAGo Gazebo simulation.

E4.evidence: Observed failure: "the JTC doesn't publish the `state` or the `controller_state` topic after starting TIAGo simulation", with printed get_node()->now() values jumping from 1.7055e+09 to 0.672.

units.name: controller_manager
units.revision_basis: The reporter states only "Version Humble" for ros2_control. a3bf2801 is the head of the ros2_control humble branch at the time the issue was opened (2024-01-17T17:33Z; last humble commit 2024-01-17T15:51Z); at that revision add_controller_impl calls controller.c->init(controller.info.name, get_namespace()) and afterwards controller.c->get_node()->set_parameter(use_sim_time), the behaviour the issue describes. The exact build the reporter ran is not stated. resolved_rev fe5b4f16 is the humble merge commit of the backport PR #1332 of #1293 (merged 2024-01-25), which moves use_sim_time into the NodeOptions arguments given to init. On master the fix is merge commit 5d4f6e7277fcd0d9a2a65b1366663e4cbf3047f2 (PR #1293).

units.name: joint_trajectory_controller
units.revision_basis: The reporter links joint_trajectory_controller.cpp at ros2_controllers commit e08dcb91 (lines 1136-1138); e08dcb91 is also the ros2_controllers humble branch head at the issue date (committed 2024-01-12, no later humble commit before 2024-01-17T17:33Z). The resolution does not change this unit, so the resolved composition keeps e08dcb91.

failed_conditions.quote: when the controllers are loaded and launched in the simulation, their node clock tends to stay in the RCL_SYSTEM_TIME` for some cycle time instead of switching to the clock of the gazebo.

loudness_evidence: No diagnostic from existing tooling; the reporter found the cause with added print statements: "We have been facing an issue for several months that the JTC doesn't publish the `state` or the `controller_state` topic after starting TIAGo simulation." and "I've added some print statements and found out the following" (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1311).

resolution.summary: controller_manager builds the controller's rclcpp::NodeOptions in a new determine_controller_node_options() and, when its own use_sim_time is true, appends "--ros-args -p use_sim_time:=true" to the arguments passed to controller.c->init(...), so the controller node is created with the simulation clock; the post-init set_parameter(use_sim_time) is removed (PR #1293, commit 201fd47c "implement logic of use_sim_time as arguments to solve #1311"; humble backport #1332).
resolution.evidence: The reporter shows a screenshot "AFTER APPLYING THE ABOVE SOLUTION" and the expected monotone sim-time values, but that was a local change passing use_sim_time in NodeOptions, not an identified revision; the merged backport #1332 was reported working in simulation by Noel215 ("Tested on simulation with https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/pull/978, as in the original PR. It is working for me.") for the parameter-loading issue, with a different ros2_controllers revision, not shown for this clock composition.

notes: Class 'other' is used because the mismatch is the time source of the controller node (system time vs simulation time) caused by the order in which the host applies use_sim_time relative to node creation; none of the listed classes (frame, unit, QoS, representation) names a clock-source/initialization-order mismatch. At e08dcb91 the controller stamps last_state_publish_time_ = get_node()->now() in on_configure (L904) and on_activate (L985), and publish_state returns early while get_node()->now() < (last_state_publish_time_ + state_publisher_period_) (L1136), so a system-time stamp followed by a switch to sim time suppresses publishing indefinitely. Inventory uses the api: form for the controller_interface base-class methods through which the host creates the plugin's node (init) and sets its parameter (get_node()->set_parameter). The /clock topic is published by Gazebo (a third unit) and is not listed. The same fix (PR #1293) also addresses other compositions that are not conditions of this case: the spawner's params-file loading into the controller node (ros2_controllers issue #966, read_only parameters and generate_parameter_library validation in on_init, ros2_controllers PRs #795/#698). Master fix: PR #1293 merge 5d4f6e72; iron backport #1331 merge 75ff3476.
